title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 8
statement: Pentagon \(ABCDE\) is inscribed in a circle, and \(\angle BEC = \angle CED = 30^\circ.\) Let \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at point \(F,\) and suppose that \(AB = 9\) and \(AD = 24.\) What is \(BF?\)

solutions.text:
The inscribed angle \(\angle BEC = 30^\circ\) subtends arc \(BC = 60^\circ,\) so \(\angle BAC,\) which also subtends arc \(BC,\) equals \(30^\circ.\) Likewise \(\angle CAD = 30^\circ.\)

Thus \(AC\) bisects \(\angle BAD = 60^\circ.\) In \(\triangle ABD,\) \[ \begin{aligned} BD^2 &= 9^2 + 24^2 \\ &\quad {}- 2(9)(24)\cos 60^\circ \\ &= 657 - 216 = 441, \end{aligned} \] so \(BD = 21.\)

Since \(AF\) (along \(AC\)) bisects \(\angle BAD,\) the Angle Bisector Theorem gives \(\dfrac{BF}{FD} = \dfrac{AB}{AD} = \dfrac{9}{24} = \dfrac{3}{8}.\) Hence \(BF = \dfrac{3}{11}\cdot 21 = \dfrac{63}{11}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: \(\angle BAC\) and \(\angle CAD\) both subtend \(30^\circ\) arcs, so \(AC\) bisects \(\angle BAD\)
Find \(BD\) with the Law of Cosines in \(\triangle ABD,\) then use the Angle Bisector Theorem
